prompt: On a street map, $A$ and $B$ are two intersections. Which notation names the stretch of street that starts at $A$, ends at $B$, and includes both intersections?
hint: The street stretch has two ends. Which symbol shows a piece with two endpoints?

hints.text: The street stretch has two ends. Which symbol shows a piece with two endpoints?
Arrows mean "keeps going forever." A plain bar means "stops at both ends."
A segment with endpoints $A$ and $B$ is written $\overline{AB}$.

explanation: A segment is a piece of a line with two endpoints, written with a plain bar: $\overline{AB}$.
$\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ has arrows on both ends, so it runs forever in both directions — a line.
$\overrightarrow{AB}$ starts at $A$ and runs forever past $B$ — a ray. And $AB$ with no bar means the length, a number.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read the arrows literally
steps: Every arrowhead is a promise that the figure keeps going that way forever.
Your stretch of street stops at two intersections, so it needs zero arrowheads: $\overline{AB}$.
